records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בִשְׁמוֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָ֣ה וְאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת שָׁנָ֡ה לְצֵ֣את בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מֵאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַיִם֩ בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הָרְבִיעִ֜ית בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ זִ֗ו ה֚וּא הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לִמְלֹ֥ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּ֥בֶן הַבַּ֖יִת לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] eightieth year and four hundred year after [the] going out of [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt, in the year the fourth, in [the] month of Ziv, that [is] the month the second, of [the] reigning of Solomon over Israel, and he built the house for Yahweh.
pieces: In the 480th year after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year that Solomon reigned over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: And it came about in the 480th year after the going out of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, that [is] the second month, of Solomon's reigning over Israel, that he built the house for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.1: Solomon began to build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the fourth year that he ruled over Israel. It was in the month of Ziv, the second month of the year, in spring. This was 480 years after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the 480th year after the exodus: a date that ties the temple to the coming out of Egypt
alternatives: twelve generations of forty years, a round figure
decisions.reason: The writer dates the founding of the temple from the exodus, so that the house of Yahweh is the goal of the journey that began in Egypt (Exodus 15:17; Deuteronomy 12:10-11). Taken as a plain count of years from Solomon's fourth year, it puts the exodus in the middle of the fifteenth century BC. Many readers of the evidence from Egypt and Canaan place it in the thirteenth century instead, and take 480 as twelve generations of forty years, a round figure for the whole period. The Hebrew gives the number without comment, and the question is not settled.

decisions.choice: four hundred and eightieth: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The early Greek translation reads "440th" here. The Hebrew number is kept; the Greek may reflect a different count of the years in the books of Joshua and Judges.

decisions.choice: the month of Ziv: the second month, April-May
decisions.reason: Ziv is an old Canaanite month name, meaning "brightness" or "bloom". The writer explains it as the second month of the year counted from the spring (Exodus 12:2), about April-May. Later the Jewish calendar called it Iyyar. It is named again in verse 37.

decisions.choice: he built the house: he began the building
decisions.reason: The verse dates the start of the work, as verse 37 says ("the foundation was laid"); verse 38 dates its completion seven years later.

decisions.choice: began to build the house of the LORD (Balanced); began to build the temple of the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: Because the verse marks the start of seven years of work (verses 37-38), Balanced and Readable say "began to build". Balanced keeps "house of the LORD" for the full phrase, as in 3:1; Readable says "temple", as in 3:1.

decisions.choice: the second month of the year, in spring
decisions.reason: Readable adds the season so that the old month name means something to the reader.

records.heading: Solomon builds the temple

records.source: וְהַבַּ֗יִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֜ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה שִׁשִּֽׁים־אַמָּ֥ה אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים רָחְבּ֑וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the house which built the king Solomon for Yahweh: sixty cubit[s] its length, and twenty its breadth, and thirty cubit[s] its height.
pieces: The temple that King Solomon built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was {{units:about 90 feet|60 cubits}} long, {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 45 feet|30 cubits}} high.

L.2: And the house which King Solomon built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 60 cubits [was] its length and 20 its breadth and 30 cubits its height.

R.2: The temple that King Solomon built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was {{units:about 90 feet|60 cubits}} long and {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide. It was {{units:about 45 feet|30 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: cubit: about 18 inches
decisions.reason: A cubit was the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 18 inches. A longer royal cubit was also used (2 Chronicles 3:3 speaks of "the former measure"), so the sizes in this chapter are approximate.

decisions.choice: the house: the main building, the hall and the inner room together
decisions.reason: The 60 cubits are the length of the main hall (40 cubits, verse 17) and the inner room (20 cubits, verse 20) together. The porch in front (verse 3) and the side rooms (verse 5) are counted separately.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: The word is "house", and Literal keeps it. In this chapter it names the building as a whole, so Balanced and Readable say "temple", keeping "house of the LORD" for the full phrase (verses 1 and 37). It is kept apart from the words for the main hall (verse 3) and the inner room (verse 5).

decisions.choice: modern measures with the cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the size in feet, reckoning a cubit at about 18 inches; the reader's Measures control shows the cubits. Literal keeps the cubits throughout this chapter.

records.source: וְהָאוּלָ֗ם עַל־פְּנֵי֙ הֵיכַ֣ל הַבַּ֔יִת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רֹ֣חַב הַבָּ֑יִת עֶ֧שֶׂר בָּאַמָּ֛ה רָחְבּ֖וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And the porch on [the] face of [the] hall of the house: twenty cubit[s] its length, on [the] face of [the] breadth of the house; ten by the cubit its breadth, on [the] face of the house.
pieces: The porch in front of the main hall of the temple was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long, matching the width of the temple, and it reached out {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} from the front of the temple.

L.3: And the porch in front of the hall of the house: 20 cubits [was] its length, along the breadth of the house; 10 cubits [was] its depth in front of the house.

R.3: In front of the main room of the temple there was a porch. It ran {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} across the whole front of the temple, and it reached out {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} from the building.

decisions.choice: the porch: the entrance hall at the front of the temple
decisions.reason: The word names the front part of the building, through which one entered (7:6-7, 12, 19, 21). It may have been an open porch or a roofed entrance room; its height is not given here. It stood at the east end, since the temple faced east (Ezekiel 8:16).

decisions.choice: the hall: the main room of the temple
decisions.reason: The word can mean a palace or a temple as a whole (Psalm 45:16; 1 Samuel 1:9). Here it names the large front room of the building, 40 cubits long (verse 17), where the priests served, as set against the inner room behind it (verse 5).

decisions.choice: length ... breadth: across the front, and outward from it
decisions.reason: The porch's "length" of 20 cubits runs along the width of the temple; its "breadth" of 10 cubits is how far it stands out from the front.

decisions.choice: porch (all levels); hall (Literal), main hall (Balanced), main room (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Porch" is a plain word for the entrance hall. "Hall" keeps the larger room apart from "temple", which Balanced and Readable use for the whole house; Balanced and Readable add "main" so that it is clear which room is meant.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לַבָּ֔יִת חַלּוֹנֵ֖י שְׁקֻפִ֥ים אֲטֻמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he made for the house windows of frames, closed.
pieces: He made windows for the temple with recessed frames.

L.4: And he made for the house windows of recessed frames.

R.4: He made windows for the temple that were set deep in their frames.

decisions.choice: windows with recessed frames
alternatives: windows narrow outside and wide inside
decisions.reason: The two words after "windows" are rare. The first seems to mean a frame or an opening framed with beams (7:4-5). The second means "closed" or "narrowed" (Ezekiel 40:16; 41:16, 26). They may describe windows set in frames that narrow as they go into the wall, windows closed with a lattice, or windows with fixed frames that could not be opened. They would have been high in the walls, above the side rooms (verses 5-6).

records.source: וַיִּבֶן֩ עַל־קִ֨יר הַבַּ֤יִת יָצִ֨יעַ֙ סָבִ֔יב אֶת־קִיר֤וֹת הַבַּ֨יִת֙ סָבִ֔יב לַֽהֵיכָ֖ל וְלַדְּבִ֑יר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ צְלָע֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he built against [the] wall of the house a side structure all around, [against] the walls of the house all around, for the hall and for the inner room; and he made side rooms all around.
pieces: Against the wall of the temple he built a side structure that ran all around it, along the walls of both the main hall and the inner sanctuary, and he made side rooms all around.

L.5: And he built against the wall of the house a side structure all around, [against] the walls of the house all around, both the hall and the inner room; and he made side chambers all around.

R.5: Solomon built a building with rooms in it against the outside walls of the temple. It went all around the main room and the inner room.

decisions.choice: side structure: the annex built around the temple
decisions.reason: The written text and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud spell this word differently (here and in verses 6 and 10), but both name the same thing: a structure built against the outer walls, holding the side rooms. Both are rare words found only in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the inner room: the most holy place at the back of the temple
alternatives: the oracle, the place of speaking
decisions.reason: The word names the innermost room of the house, where the ark was placed (verses 16, 19-20; 8:6). It may come from a word for "back" or "rear"; an older explanation linked it with "speak", as the place of God's word, but this is less likely. Verse 16 calls it "the most holy place".

decisions.choice: side rooms: storerooms in stories along the walls
decisions.reason: The word means "side" or "rib" (Genesis 2:21). Here it names rooms built in three stories (verses 6, 8, 10), probably used to store temple goods and gifts (7:51).

decisions.choice: side structure; inner room (Literal), inner sanctuary (Balanced), inner room (Readable); side chambers (Literal), side rooms (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable call the innermost room the "inner room", which says plainly where it was. Balanced says "inner sanctuary" so that it is clear it is the holiest place, not a storeroom.

decisions.choice: a building with rooms in it
decisions.reason: Readable puts the side structure and its rooms together in one plain description.

records.source: הַיָּצִ֨יעַ הַתַּחְתֹּנָ֜ה חָמֵ֧שׁ בָּאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבָּ֗הּ וְהַתִּֽיכֹנָה֙ שֵׁ֤שׁ בָּֽאַמָּה֙ רָחְבָּ֔הּ וְהַ֨שְּׁלִישִׁ֔ית שֶׁ֥בַע בָּאַמָּ֖ה רָחְבָּ֑הּ כִּ֡י מִגְרָעוֹת֩ נָתַ֨ן לַבַּ֤יִת סָבִיב֙ ח֔וּצָה לְבִלְתִּ֖י אֲחֹ֥ז בְּקִֽירוֹת־הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: The side structure the lowest: five by the cubit its breadth; and the middle: six by the cubit its breadth; and the third: seven by the cubit its breadth; for ledges he made for the house all around outside, so as not to grasp into [the] walls of the house.
pieces: The lowest story was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} wide, the middle one {{units:about 9 feet|6 cubits}} wide, and the third {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|7 cubits}} wide. He had made ledges around the outside of the temple wall, so that the beams would not be set into the walls of the temple.

L.6: The lowest [story of the] side structure, 5 cubits [was] its breadth, and the middle six cubits its breadth, and the third seven cubits its breadth; for he made ledges for the house all around outside, so that [the beams] would not grasp into the walls of the house.

R.6: The rooms on the ground floor were {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} wide. The rooms on the middle floor were {{units:about 9 feet|6 cubits}} wide, and the rooms on the top floor were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|7 cubits}} wide. This was because the temple wall became thinner at each floor, leaving a ledge all around the outside. The beams of the side building rested on these ledges, so they did not have to be cut into the temple walls.

decisions.choice: the side structure: as in verse 5
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the written text and the form read aloud spell the word differently. The feminine words that follow ("lowest", "middle", "third") speak of its stories.

decisions.choice: ledges: the temple wall stepped in at each story, and the beams of the side rooms rested on the steps
decisions.reason: The temple wall was thickest at the bottom and stepped back one cubit at each story. The floor beams of the side rooms rested on these ledges instead of being set into holes in the temple wall. That is why each story is one cubit wider than the one below.

decisions.choice: [the beams] (Literal); the beams (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say what would not be fastened into the walls; from the building method it is the beams of the side rooms.

decisions.choice: the temple wall became thinner at each floor
decisions.reason: Readable explains how the ledges made each floor wider than the one below, which the Hebrew leaves the reader to work out.

records.source: וְהַבַּ֨יִת֙ בְּהִבָּ֣נֹת֔וֹ אֶֽבֶן־שְׁלֵמָ֥ה מַסָּ֖ע נִבְנָ֑ה וּמַקָּב֤וֹת וְהַגַּרְזֶן֙ כָּל־כְּלִ֣י בַרְזֶ֔ל לֹֽא־נִשְׁמַ֥ע בַּבַּ֖יִת בְּהִבָּנֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the house, in its being built, [of] stone finished [at the] quarry it was built; and hammers and the axe, any tool of iron, not was heard in the house in its being built.
pieces: The temple was built of stone that had been dressed at the quarry, so the sound of hammer, axe or any iron tool was never heard at the temple during the building.

L.7: And the house, when it was built, was built [of] stone finished at the quarry; and hammers and axe, any tool of iron, was not heard in the house when it was built.

R.7: The stones used to build the temple were cut and shaped at the place where they were dug out. So while the temple was being built, no one heard the sound of a hammer, an axe, or any other iron tool there.

decisions.choice: stone finished at the quarry: blocks cut to shape before they were brought
decisions.reason: The phrase is short: "whole stone, quarry". It means stone dressed to its final shape where it was quarried (5:31-32), so that it only had to be set in place.

decisions.choice: no iron tool heard: the temple built in quietness
decisions.reason: The law said an altar must be of uncut stones on which no iron tool had been used (Exodus 20:25; Deuteronomy 27:5). Here the stones are cut, but away from the site, so the holy place was built without the noise of tools. The text does not say why; the silence fits the holiness of the house.

decisions.choice: so no hammer ... was heard
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses with "so", since the second follows from the first.

records.source: פֶּ֗תַח הַצֵּלָע֙ הַתִּ֣יכֹנָ֔ה אֶל־כֶּ֥תֶף הַבַּ֖יִת הַיְמָנִ֑ית וּבְלוּלִּ֗ים יַֽעֲלוּ֙ עַל־הַתִּ֣יכֹנָ֔ה וּמִן־הַתִּֽיכֹנָ֖ה אֶל־הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: [The] entrance of the side room the middle [was] at [the] side of the house the right; and by stairways they would go up to the middle, and from the middle to the third.
pieces: The entrance to the middle story of side rooms was on the south side of the temple, and stairways led up to the middle story and from the middle to the third.

L.8: The entrance of the middle side chamber [was] on the right side of the house; and by stairways they went up to the middle [story], and from the middle to the third.

R.8: The way into the side rooms was on the south side of the temple. From there, stairs led up to the middle floor, and from the middle floor to the top floor.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the middle side room: the Hebrew text
alternatives: the entrance of the lowest story
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the entrance was to the "middle" side room. The early Greek translation reads "lowest", which fits the stairways that lead up from it to the middle story. The Hebrew may mean the entrance in the middle of the side structure's south wall. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: the right side: the south side
decisions.reason: Facing east, the direction the temple faced, the right hand is the south (7:39).

decisions.choice: stairways: probably winding stairs
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may mean winding stairs, ladders, or shafts with trapdoors between the floors. Whatever its exact form, it was a way up from story to story.

decisions.choice: the south side
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "right"; Balanced and Readable give the direction it means.

decisions.choice: the way into the side rooms
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the entrance without the question about which story it opened onto, which the footnote on the meaning decision explains.

records.source: וַיִּ֥בֶן אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת וַיְכַלֵּ֑הוּ וַיִּסְפֹּ֤ן אֶת־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ גֵּבִ֔ים וּשְׂדֵרֹ֖ת בָּאֲרָזִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he built the house and finished it, and he covered the house [with] beams and rows of cedars.
pieces: So he built the temple and finished it, and he roofed it with beams and planks of cedar.

L.9: And he built the house and finished it; and he covered the house [with] beams and rows of cedar.

R.9: So Solomon built the temple and finished it. He made its roof out of cedar beams and boards.

decisions.choice: covered the house with beams and rows of cedar: roofed it
decisions.reason: The verb means to cover over, and is used of a roof or a ceiling (7:3, 7). The second noun means "rows" or "ranks" and may name planks laid in rows over the beams. It probably describes the roof, though it could mean a paneled ceiling inside.

decisions.choice: built ... and finished it: a summary of the outer building
decisions.reason: Verses 9 and 14 sum up the building of the outside; the chapter then turns to the inside and its decoration (verses 15-36). The work was finished only in the eleventh year (verse 38).

records.source: וַיִּ֤בֶן אֶת־הַיָּצִ֨יעַ֙ עַל־כָּל־הַבַּ֔יִת חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֽוֹמָת֑וֹ וַיֶּאֱחֹ֥ז אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת בַּעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And he built the side structure against all the house, five cubits its height, and it held the house with timbers of cedars.
pieces: He built the side structure against the whole temple, each story {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high, and joined it to the temple with cedar beams.

L.10: And he built the side structure against all the house, 5 cubits its height, and it was fastened to the house with timbers of cedar.

R.10: He built the side rooms all along the temple. Each floor was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high. Cedar beams joined this building to the temple.

decisions.choice: the side structure: as in verse 5
decisions.reason: As in verses 5 and 6, the written text and the form read aloud spell the word differently.

decisions.choice: five cubits its height: the height of each story
alternatives: the height of the whole side structure
decisions.reason: With three stories (verse 6), five cubits is the height of each story, not of the whole structure. The Hebrew says only "five cubits its height".

decisions.choice: it held the house: the side structure was joined to the temple
decisions.reason: The verb means "take hold of". The subject may be Solomon ("he fastened it") or the side structure; either way the annex was joined to the temple by cedar beams resting on the ledges of verse 6.

decisions.choice: each story (Balanced); each floor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the height is that of each story, following meaning decision m2.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Solomon, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Solomon:

L.11: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Solomon, saying,

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Solomon this message:

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came: a message from God
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual way of saying that Yahweh spoke to someone, often through a prophet (2 Samuel 7:4; 24:11). The text does not say how it came to Solomon here.

decisions.choice: gave Solomon this message
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the LORD spoke to Solomon.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} speaks to Solomon

records.source: הַבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה בֹנֶ֗ה אִם־תֵּלֵ֤ךְ בְּחֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֣י תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֥ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתַ֖י לָלֶ֣כֶת בָּהֶ֑ם וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־דְּבָרִי֙ אִתָּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: The house the this which you [are] building, if you will walk in my statutes, and my judgments you will do, and you will keep all my commandments to walk in them, and I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father,
pieces: "As for this house you are building, if you live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments by following them, I will carry out through you the word I gave to David your father,

L.12: "[As for] this house which you are building: if you walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments and keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, walking in them, then I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word with you, which I spoke to David your father,

R.12: "You are building this temple. If you follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws, obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules, and keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, then I will do for you what I promised your father David.

decisions.choice: this house which you are building: the subject the promise is set beside
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with the house and then breaks off into a condition about Solomon's life. The effect is to set the building beside obedience: the house matters, but the promise depends on keeping Yahweh's commands.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments, commandments: the whole of Yahweh's law
decisions.reason: The three words together cover all that Yahweh commanded, as in Deuteronomy 5:31 and 1 Kings 2:3. "Walk in" means to live by them.

decisions.choice: my word which I spoke to David: the promise of a lasting house and throne
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised David that his son would build a house for his name and that his throne would last (2 Samuel 7:12-16). David passed on the condition to Solomon (2:4). Here Yahweh repeats it while the temple is being built.

decisions.choice: and I will establish: the result of the condition
decisions.reason: The "and" introduces what follows if Solomon obeys: "then I will establish".

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments, commandments (Literal); statutes, rulings, commandments (Balanced); laws, rules, commands (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus and Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: carry out the word I gave (Balanced); do what I promised (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Establish my word" means to make a promise stand by carrying it out; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְשָׁ֣כַנְתִּ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א אֶעֱזֹ֖ב אֶת־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: and I will dwell in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel, and not I will forsake my people Israel.
pieces: and I will live among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and will not abandon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel."

L.13: and I will dwell among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and I will not forsake {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel."

R.13: I will live among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and I will never leave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel."

decisions.choice: I will dwell among: Yahweh's presence with his people
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Yahweh living among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8; 29:45). The promise is not that the building holds Yahweh (8:27), but that he will live among his people.

decisions.choice: and I will not forsake: part of the promise that depends on obedience
decisions.reason: This clause still follows the "if" of verse 12: Yahweh's dwelling and faithfulness are promised along with the call to obey (9:6-9).

records.source: וַיִּ֧בֶן שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת וַיְכַלֵּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And built Solomon the house and finished it.
pieces: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.

L.14: And Solomon built the house and finished it.

R.14: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.

decisions.choice: built ... and finished it: taking up verse 9 again
decisions.reason: After the word of Yahweh, the narrator returns to the building with the same words as verse 9, and then describes the inside.

records.heading: The inside of the temple

records.source: וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־קִיר֨וֹת הַבַּ֤יִת מִבַּ֨יְתָה֙ בְּצַלְע֣וֹת אֲרָזִ֔ים מִקַּרְקַ֤ע הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַד־קִיר֣וֹת הַסִּפֻּ֔ן צִפָּ֥ה עֵ֖ץ מִבָּ֑יִת וַיְצַ֛ף אֶת־קַרְקַ֥ע הַבַּ֖יִת בְּצַלְע֥וֹת בְּרוֹשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And he built the walls of the house from inside with boards of cedars; from [the] floor of the house to [the] walls of the ceiling he overlaid [with] wood inside; and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypresses.
pieces: He lined the inside walls of the temple with cedar boards, paneling them with wood from the floor of the temple up to the rafters of the ceiling, and he covered the floor of the temple with boards of cypress.

L.15: And he lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling he covered [them with] wood inside; and he covered the floor of the house with boards of cypress.

R.15: Inside the temple, Solomon covered the walls with cedar boards from the floor all the way up to the ceiling. He covered the floor with boards of cypress wood.

decisions.choice: the rafters of the ceiling
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the walls of the ceiling". A change of one vowel letter gives "the beams of the ceiling", which the early Greek translation supports and which fits the sense. Either way the paneling reached from floor to ceiling.

decisions.choice: cypress: a tall evergreen tree used for building
decisions.reason: The tree is a cypress, juniper or fir, a strong wood from Lebanon sent with the cedar (5:22, 24). Its exact kind is not certain.

decisions.choice: lined (all levels); covered (Literal); paneling, covered (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The verb "built" with "boards" means to line the walls. The other verb means to overlay, the word used for overlaying with gold (verses 20-22); with wood it is "covered" or "paneled".

records.source: וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים אַמָּ֜ה מִֽיַּרְכְּתֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ בְּצַלְע֣וֹת אֲרָזִ֔ים מִן־הַקַּרְקַ֖ע עַד־הַקִּיר֑וֹת וַיִּ֤בֶן לוֹ֙ מִבַּ֣יִת לִדְבִ֔יר לְקֹ֖דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And he built twenty cubit[s] from [the] back of the house with boards of cedars, from the floor to the walls; and he built [it] for it inside, for an inner room, for [the] holy of the holies.
pieces: He partitioned off {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} at the back of the temple with cedar boards from the floor to the rafters, and built it inside as the inner sanctuary, the most holy place.

L.16: And he built 20 cubits from the back of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor to the rafters; and he built [it] inside as an inner room, as the holy of holies.

R.16: At the back of the temple he walled off a room {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} deep, using cedar boards from the floor to the ceiling. This was the inner room, the most holy place.

decisions.choice: from the back of the house
decisions.reason: The written text and the form read aloud differ slightly in spelling; both mean "from the back parts of the house".

decisions.choice: built 20 cubits from the back: a cedar partition closing off the inner room
decisions.reason: The 20 cubits at the back of the 60-cubit house (verse 2) were closed off by a wall of cedar from floor to ceiling, making the inner room 20 cubits deep (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the holy of holies: the most holy place
decisions.reason: The phrase means the holiest place of all, as for the inner room of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:33-34). It was where the ark stood (verse 19) and where only the high priest went, once a year (Leviticus 16).

decisions.choice: the rafters
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, the Hebrew reads "the walls"; the sense is the beams of the ceiling.

decisions.choice: the holy of holies (Literal); the most holy place (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 26:33-34.

decisions.choice: partitioned off (Balanced); walled off (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "built"; Balanced and Readable say what the building did.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים בָּאַמָּ֖ה הָיָ֣ה הַבָּ֑יִת ה֖וּא הַהֵיכָ֥ל לִפְנָֽי׃
records.gloss: And forty by the cubit was the house, that [is] the hall, before [it].
pieces: The rest of the temple, the main hall in front of the inner sanctuary, was {{units:about 60 feet|40 cubits}} long.

L.17: And the house was 40 cubits, that [is], the hall in front [of it].

R.17: The main room in front of the inner room was {{units:about 60 feet|40 cubits}} long.

decisions.choice: before: in front of the inner room
decisions.reason: The last word is an unusual form of "before", pointed in the Hebrew as if it meant "before me". The sense is that the hall lay in front of the inner room, toward the entrance. Some take the form as a name for the hall, "the front room".

decisions.choice: the rest of the temple ... in front of the inner sanctuary
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly that these 40 cubits are the part of the house left after the inner room was closed off.

records.source: וְאֶ֤רֶז אֶל־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ פְּנִ֔ימָה מִקְלַ֣עַת פְּקָעִ֔ים וּפְטוּרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים הַכֹּ֣ל אֶ֔רֶז אֵ֥ין אֶ֖בֶן נִרְאָֽה׃
records.gloss: And cedar for the house within [was] carving of gourds and opened [things] of blossoms; the whole [was] cedar; not stone was seen.
pieces: Inside, the temple's cedar was carved with gourds and open flowers. It was all cedar; no stone showed.

L.18: And cedar [was on] the house within, carved [with] gourds and open flowers; all [was] cedar; no stone was seen.

R.18: The cedar on the inside walls had carvings of gourds and open flowers. Everything was covered with cedar, so none of the stone could be seen.

decisions.choice: gourds: round, fruit-like ornaments
decisions.reason: The word is related to the wild gourds of 2 Kings 4:39. Here it names a carved ornament of that shape, perhaps in a row like a band (7:24).

decisions.choice: open flowers: carved blossoms
decisions.reason: The phrase is "openings of blossoms": flowers in full bloom, carved in the wood, as in verses 29, 32 and 35.

records.source: וּדְבִ֧יר בְּתוֹךְ־הַבַּ֛יִת מִפְּנִ֖ימָה הֵכִ֑ין לְתִתֵּ֣ן שָׁ֔ם אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן בְּרִ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] inner room in [the] midst of the house within he prepared, to put there [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh.
pieces: He prepared the inner sanctuary inside the temple to place the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there.

L.19: And he prepared the inner room inside, in the midst of the house, to put there the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.19: He got the inner room ready inside the temple as the place for the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant, the chest that held the covenant tablets.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant of Yahweh: the chest that held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: The ark was the gold-covered chest made at Sinai to hold the tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:10-22; Deuteronomy 10:1-5). Solomon brings it into the inner room in 8:6.

decisions.choice: the chest that held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ark" once in this chapter, keeping the word itself.

records.source: וְלִפְנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֡יר עֶשְׂרִים֩ אַמָּ֨ה אֹ֜רֶךְ וְעֶשְׂרִ֧ים אַמָּ֣ה רֹ֗חַב וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים אַמָּה֙ קֽוֹמָת֔וֹ וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר וַיְצַ֥ף מִזְבֵּ֖חַ אָֽרֶז׃
records.gloss: And [the] front of the inner room: twenty cubit[s] length, and twenty cubit[s] breadth, and twenty cubit[s] its height; and he overlaid it [with] gold refined; and he overlaid an altar [of] cedar.
pieces: The inner sanctuary was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long, {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} high, and he overlaid it with pure gold. He also overlaid an altar of cedar.

L.20: And the inside of the inner room [was] 20 cubits length and 20 cubits breadth and 20 cubits its height; and he overlaid it [with] pure gold; and he overlaid an altar of cedar.

R.20: The inner room was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long, {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide, and {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} high. Solomon covered it with pure gold. He also covered an altar made of cedar wood.

decisions.choice: the front of the inner room: the inner room itself
alternatives: and in front of the inner room
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins "and before the inner room", which does not fit the measurements that follow. It is best taken as a heading, "the inner room in front", or read with a small change as "the inside of the inner room". Either way the measurements are those of the room itself, a perfect cube.

decisions.choice: twenty cubits each way: a cube
decisions.reason: The inner room was as long, as wide and as high as it was long. Since the house was 30 cubits high (verse 2), its floor may have been raised or its ceiling lowered. The inner room of the temple in Ezekiel's vision is also twenty cubits square (Ezekiel 41:4).

decisions.choice: pure gold: refined gold
decisions.reason: The second word means "closed" or "shut up" and is used for gold of the best quality (7:49-50; 10:21).

decisions.choice: an altar of cedar: the incense altar, overlaid with gold
alternatives: he covered the altar with cedar
decisions.reason: This is the altar that stood before the inner room, where incense was burned (7:48; Exodus 30:1-6). It was made of cedar and overlaid with gold (verse 22). The early Greek translation reads "he made an altar".

decisions.choice: overlaid (Literal, Balanced); covered (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 25:11 and 25:24.

records.source: וַיְצַ֨ף שְׁלֹמֹ֧ה אֶת־הַבַּ֛יִת מִפְּנִ֖ימָה זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר וַיְעַבֵּ֞ר בְּרַתּוּק֤וֹת זָהָב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֔יר וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And overlaid Solomon the house within [with] gold refined, and he drew across with chains of gold before the inner room, and he overlaid it [with] gold.
pieces: Inside the temple Solomon overlaid everything with pure gold. He drew gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which he also overlaid with gold.

L.21: And Solomon overlaid the house within [with] pure gold, and he drew chains of gold across in front of the inner room, and he overlaid it [with] gold.

R.21: Solomon covered the inside of the temple with pure gold. He hung gold chains across the front of the inner room, which was covered with gold too.

decisions.choice: with chains of gold
decisions.reason: The written text and the form read aloud differ in a small detail of spelling; the sense "with chains" is the same.

decisions.choice: drew chains of gold across in front of the inner room
decisions.reason: The chains probably stretched across the entrance to the inner room, perhaps holding a curtain (2 Chronicles 3:14). The exact arrangement is not clear.

decisions.choice: he overlaid it with gold: the inner room
decisions.reason: "It" is most likely the inner room just named, as verse 20 says; it could also be the cedar partition across which the chains were drawn.

records.source: וְאֶת־כָּל־הַבַּ֛יִת צִפָּ֥ה זָהָ֖ב עַד־תֹּ֣ם כָּל־הַבָּ֑יִת וְכָל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ אֲֽשֶׁר־לַדְּבִ֖יר צִפָּ֥ה זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And all the house he overlaid [with] gold, until [the] finishing of all the house; and all the altar which [belonged] to the inner room he overlaid [with] gold.
pieces: So he overlaid the whole temple with gold until it was all finished. He also overlaid with gold the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.

L.22: And all the house he overlaid [with] gold, until all the house was finished; and the whole altar which [belonged] to the inner room he overlaid [with] gold.

R.22: In this way he covered the whole inside of the temple with gold until it was all done. He also covered with gold the altar that belonged to the inner room.

decisions.choice: the altar which belonged to the inner room: the incense altar
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. The altar stood in the main hall, in front of the inner room, but it served the inner room, so it is said to belong to it (compare Hebrews 9:4).

decisions.choice: all the house: the inside of the building
decisions.reason: After verse 21, "all the house" means the whole interior, both the hall and the inner room.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בַּדְּבִ֔יר שְׁנֵ֥י כְרוּבִ֖ים עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת קוֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he made in the inner room two cherubim [of] wood of oil; ten cubits its height.
pieces: He made two cherubim of olive wood for the inner sanctuary, each {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} high.

L.23: And he made in the inner room two cherubim [of] olive wood; 10 cubits [was] the height of each.

R.23: In the inner room Solomon made two cherubim out of olive wood. Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures. Each one was {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} tall.

decisions.choice: cherubim: winged heavenly beings who guard God's presence
decisions.reason: Cherubim guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24), stood over the ark in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:18-22), and are described as bearing God's throne (Psalm 18:11; Ezekiel 10). These two stand in the inner room over the ark (8:6-7).

decisions.choice: olive wood
decisions.reason: The phrase is "wood of oil", meaning an oil-rich tree. It is usually taken as the olive, though in Nehemiah 8:15 it is listed apart from the olive and may be a kind of wild olive or pine.

decisions.choice: Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 25:18, Readable explains the word once.

records.source: וְחָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֗וֹת כְּנַ֤ף הַכְּרוּב֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וְחָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת כְּנַ֥ף הַכְּר֖וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֔וֹת מִקְצ֥וֹת כְּנָפָ֖יו וְעַד־קְצ֥וֹת כְּנָפָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And five cubits [the] wing of the cherub the one, and five cubits [the] wing of the cherub the second; ten cubits from [the] ends of his wings and to [the] ends of his wings.
pieces: One wing of the cherub was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} long and the other wing {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}}, so its wings spanned {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} from wingtip to wingtip.

L.24: And 5 cubits [was] the one wing of the cherub, and 5 cubits the other wing of the cherub; 10 cubits from the tip of one of his wings to the tip of the other.

R.24: Each cherub had two wings, and each wing was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} long. So its wings reached {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} from one wingtip to the other.

decisions.choice: the one wing of the cherub and the other wing
decisions.reason: "One" and "second" describe the wings, not the cherubim: each cherub had two wings of five cubits, so its wingspan was ten cubits.

records.source: וְעֶ֨שֶׂר֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה הַכְּר֖וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֑י מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת וְקֶ֥צֶב אֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And ten by the cubit the cherub the second; one measure and one shape [belonged] to [the] two of the cherubim.
pieces: The second cherub also measured {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}}. The two cherubim were the same size and the same shape.

L.25: And the second cherub [was] 10 cubits; the two cherubim [had] one measure and one shape.

R.25: The second cherub also had wings that measured {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} from tip to tip. The two cherubim were exactly the same in size and shape.

decisions.choice: the second cherub ten cubits: its wingspan, as in verse 24
decisions.reason: Following verse 24, the ten cubits are the second cherub's wingspan; verse 26 gives the height.

decisions.choice: had wings that measured ... from tip to tip
decisions.reason: Readable says what was measured, following verse 24.

records.source: קוֹמַת֙ הַכְּר֣וּב הָֽאֶחָ֔ד עֶ֖שֶׂר בָּֽאַמָּ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן הַכְּר֥וּב הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃
records.gloss: [The] height of the cherub the one [was] ten by the cubit, and so the cherub the second.
pieces: The height of one cherub was {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}}, and so was the other.

L.26: The height of the one cherub [was] 10 cubits, and so [was] the second cherub.

R.26: Each cherub was {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} tall.

decisions.choice: the height: as in verse 23
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the height given in verse 23, closing the description of the two figures: they were as tall as their wingspan and half the height of the room.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֶת־הַכְּרוּבִ֜ים בְּת֣וֹךְ׀הַבַּ֣יִת הַפְּנִימִ֗י וַֽיִּפְרְשׂוּ֮ אֶת־כַּנְפֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִים֒ וַתִּגַּ֤ע כְּנַף־הָֽאֶחָד֙ בַּקִּ֔יר וּכְנַף֙ הַכְּר֣וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֔י נֹגַ֖עַת בַּקִּ֣יר הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַבַּ֔יִת נֹגְעֹ֖ת כָּנָ֥ף אֶל־כָּנָֽף׃
records.gloss: And he put the cherubim in [the] midst of the house the inner; and they spread out the wings of the cherubim, and touched [the] wing of the one against the wall, and [the] wing of the cherub the second [was] touching against the wall the second; and their wings to [the] midst of the house [were] touching wing to wing.
pieces: He placed the cherubim in the middle of the inner sanctuary of the temple. Their wings were spread out, so that the wing of one touched one wall and the wing of the other touched the other wall, while their wings met each other in the middle of the room.

L.27: And he put the cherubim in the midst of the inner house; and the wings of the cherubim were spread out, so that the wing of the one touched the wall, and the wing of the second cherub was touching the other wall; and their wings in the middle of the house were touching, wing to wing.

R.27: He put the cherubim in the middle of the inner room. Their wings were spread out. One wing of the first cherub touched one side wall, and one wing of the second cherub touched the other side wall. Their other wings touched each other in the middle of the room.

decisions.choice: they spread out the wings: the wings were spread
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means the wings stood spread out. Side by side, the two wingspans of ten cubits filled the twenty-cubit width of the room (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the inner house: the inner room, where the cherubim overshadowed the ark
decisions.reason: "The inner house" is the inner room. Unlike the tabernacle cherubim, which faced each other on the ark's cover (Exodus 25:20), these stood on the floor facing the hall (2 Chronicles 3:13), and the ark was set under their wings (8:6-7).

decisions.choice: the inner sanctuary (Balanced); the inner room (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the inner house"; Balanced and Readable name the room.

records.source: וַיְצַ֥ף אֶת־הַכְּרוּבִ֖ים זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And he overlaid the cherubim [with] gold.
pieces: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.

L.28: And he overlaid the cherubim [with] gold.

R.28: He covered the cherubim with gold.

decisions.choice: overlaid the cherubim with gold: gold over wood
decisions.reason: The olive-wood figures (verse 23) were overlaid with gold, as the ark and its poles were (Exodus 25:11, 13).

records.source: וְאֵת֩ כָּל־קִיר֨וֹת הַבַּ֜יִת מֵסַ֣ב׀קָלַ֗ע פִּתּוּחֵי֙ מִקְלְעוֹת֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים וְתִֽמֹרֹ֔ת וּפְטוּרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים מִלִּפְנִ֖ים וְלַחִיצֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And all [the] walls of the house round about he carved [with] engravings of carvings of cherubim and palm trees and opened [things] of blossoms, from within and to the outer.
pieces: On all the walls of the temple, all around, in both the inner and the outer rooms, he carved figures of cherubim, palm trees and open flowers.

L.29: And on all the walls of the house round about he carved engraved figures of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, in the inner and outer [rooms].

R.29: On all the walls around the temple, in both the inner room and the main room, he carved pictures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.

decisions.choice: from within and to the outer: the inner room and the main hall
decisions.reason: The phrase is short: "from inside and to the outer". It means both rooms, the inner room and the main hall in front of it, as in verse 30.

decisions.choice: cherubim, palm trees and flowers: a picture of a garden
decisions.reason: Cherubim, trees and blossoms recall the garden of Eden, which cherubim guarded (Genesis 2-3). The same figures decorate Ezekiel's temple (Ezekiel 41:18-20). The text does not explain the meaning of the carvings.

decisions.choice: [rooms] (Literal); rooms (Balanced); the inner room and the main room (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not repeat the noun; English needs it.

records.source: וְאֶת־קַרְקַ֥ע הַבַּ֖יִת צִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֑ב לִפְנִ֖ימָה וְלַחִיצֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And [the] floor of the house he overlaid [with] gold, to within and to the outer.
pieces: He also overlaid the floor of the temple with gold, in both the inner and the outer rooms.

L.30: And the floor of the house he overlaid [with] gold, in the inner and outer [rooms].

R.30: He covered the floor of the temple with gold too, in both the inner room and the main room.

decisions.choice: to within and to the outer: as in verse 29
decisions.reason: Both rooms, the inner room and the main hall.

records.source: וְאֵת֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַדְּבִ֔יר עָשָׂ֖ה דַּלְת֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן הָאַ֥יִל מְזוּז֖וֹת חֲמִשִֽׁית׃
records.gloss: And [for] the entrance of the inner room he made doors of wood of oil; the lintel, doorposts, fifth.
pieces: He made doors of olive wood for the entrance to the inner sanctuary, with a lintel and doorposts forming a five-sided frame.

L.31: And for the entrance of the inner room he made doors of olive wood; the lintel [and] doorposts [were] five-sided.

R.31: For the doorway into the inner room he made doors of olive wood. The frame of the doorway had five sides.

decisions.choice: the lintel and doorposts were five-sided
alternatives: a frame of five recessed steps
a fifth of the wall's width
decisions.reason: The words are short and unclear: "the lintel, doorposts, fifth". They may mean that the doorframe had five sides (a pointed or stepped top over the posts), that its frame was set in five steps, or that the doorway took up a fifth of the width of the wall. The first is followed here.

decisions.choice: olive wood: as in verse 23
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

decisions.choice: the frame of the doorway
decisions.reason: Readable uses one plain word for the lintel and doorposts together.

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּי֮ דַּלְת֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שֶׁמֶן֒ וְקָלַ֣ע עֲ֠לֵיהֶם מִקְלְע֨וֹת כְּרוּבִ֧ים וְתִמֹר֛וֹת וּפְטוּרֵ֥י צִצִּ֖ים וְצִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֑ב וַיָּ֛רֶד עַל־הַכְּרוּבִ֥ים וְעַל־הַתִּֽמֹר֖וֹת אֶת־הַזָּהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And two doors of wood of oil; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and opened [things] of blossoms, and he overlaid [them with] gold, and he spread on the cherubim and on the palm trees the gold.
pieces: On the two olive-wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold, beating the gold down onto the cherubim and the palm trees.

L.32: And the two doors [were] of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid [them with] gold, and spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.

R.32: On the two olive-wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers. Then he covered the doors with gold, pressing the gold down onto the shapes of the cherubim and palm trees.

decisions.choice: spread the gold: beaten down onto the carvings
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring down or beat out. The gold was hammered thin over the carved figures so that their shapes showed through.

records.source: וְכֵ֥ן עָשָׂ֛ה לְפֶ֥תַח הַֽהֵיכָ֖ל מְזוּז֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן מֵאֵ֖ת רְבִעִֽית׃
records.gloss: And so he made for [the] entrance of the hall doorposts of wood of oil, from with a fourth.
pieces: In the same way he made doorposts of olive wood for the entrance of the main hall, in a four-sided frame.

L.33: And so he made for the entrance of the hall doorposts of olive wood, from a fourth.

R.33: He did the same thing for the doorway of the main room. He made its doorposts of olive wood, in a frame with four sides.

decisions.choice: from a fourth: a four-sided frame
alternatives: a frame of four recessed steps
a quarter of the wall's width
decisions.reason: As with verse 31, the phrase is short and unclear: "from with a fourth". It may mean a four-sided (square) frame, a frame of four steps, or a doorway taking up a quarter of the wall. The first is followed here, matching the choice in verse 31.

decisions.choice: from a fourth
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare phrase, since its sense is uncertain.

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י דַלְת֖וֹת עֲצֵ֣י בְרוֹשִׁ֑ים שְׁנֵ֨י צְלָעִ֜ים הַדֶּ֤לֶת הָֽאַחַת֙ גְּלִילִ֔ים וּשְׁנֵ֧י קְלָעִ֛ים הַדֶּ֥לֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית גְּלִילִֽים׃
records.gloss: And two doors [of] wood of cypresses; two leaves of the door the one [were] turning, and two leaves of the door the second [were] turning.
pieces: The two doors were of cypress wood. Each door had two leaves that folded.

L.34: And two doors [of] cypress wood; two leaves of the one door [were] folding, and two leaves of the other door [were] folding.

R.34: There were two doors made of cypress wood. Each door was made of two parts that folded back.

decisions.choice: two folding leaves: each door made in two parts that turned
decisions.reason: The word for "turning" is used of things that roll or turn. Each door was made of two panels that could fold back on each other or turn on pivots, so that a large doorway could be opened in part.

decisions.choice: leaves
decisions.reason: The second time, the Hebrew has a word that elsewhere means "hangings" (Exodus 27:9). It differs by one letter from the word for "leaves" earlier in the verse, and most likely the same word is meant both times.

records.source: וְקָלַ֤ע כְּרוּבִים֙ וְתִ֣מֹר֔וֹת וּפְטֻרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים וְצִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֔ב מְיֻשָּׁ֖ר עַל־הַמְּחֻקֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he carved cherubim and palm trees and opened [things] of blossoms, and he overlaid [with] gold made even on the carved [work].
pieces: He carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers on them, and overlaid them with gold fitted evenly over the carving.

L.35: And he carved cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and he overlaid [them with] gold fitted evenly on the carved work.

R.35: He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them. Then he covered them with gold that fit smoothly over the carvings.

decisions.choice: gold made even on the carved work: gold laid smoothly over the carving
decisions.reason: The gold was fitted closely and evenly over the carved figures, as in verse 32.

records.source: וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔ית שְׁלֹשָׁ֖ה טוּרֵ֣י גָזִ֑ית וְט֖וּר כְּרֻתֹ֥ת אֲרָזִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he built the court the inner [with] three rows of hewn [stone] and a row of beams of cedars.
pieces: He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams.

L.36: And he built the inner court [with] three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams.

R.36: He built a wall around the inner courtyard. He used three layers of cut stone and then one layer of cedar beams.

decisions.choice: the inner court: the courtyard around the temple
decisions.reason: This is the court around the temple itself, where the bronze altar and basin stood (8:64; 2 Kings 23:12), as distinct from the great court that also took in the palace (7:9-12).

decisions.choice: three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams: a wall built in layers
decisions.reason: The wall of the court was built of courses of cut stone with a course of timber laid over them, a method that strengthened the wall (7:12; Ezra 6:4).

decisions.choice: a wall around
decisions.reason: The rows of stone and beams describe the court's wall; Readable says so.

records.source: בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית יֻסַּ֖ד בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּיֶ֖רַח זִֽו׃
records.gloss: In the year the fourth was founded [the] house of Yahweh, in [the] month of Ziv.
pieces: In the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, the foundation of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was laid.

L.37: In the fourth year the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was founded, in the month of Ziv.

R.37: The foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was laid in the fourth year that Solomon ruled, in the month of Ziv.

decisions.choice: the fourth year: of Solomon's reign, as in verse 1
decisions.reason: Verses 37-38 sum up the dates: the foundation in the fourth year (verse 1) and the completion in the eleventh.

decisions.choice: the month of Ziv: as in verse 1
decisions.reason: The second month, about April-May.

decisions.choice: that Solomon ruled
decisions.reason: Readable says whose fourth year, from verse 1.

records.source: וּבַשָּׁנָה֩ הָאַחַ֨ת עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה בְּיֶ֣רַח בּ֗וּל ה֚וּא הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י כָּלָ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְכָל־דְּבָרָ֖יו וּלְכָל־מִשְׁפָּטָ֑יו וַיִּבְנֵ֖הוּ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And in the year the eleventh, in [the] month of Bul, that [is] the month the eighth, was finished the house in all its parts and in all its plans; and he built it seven years.
pieces: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the temple was finished in all its parts and just as it had been planned. He had been seven years building it.

L.38: And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, that [is] the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts and in all its plans; and he built it [in] seven years.

R.38: The temple was finished in the eleventh year that Solomon ruled. It was in the month of Bul, the eighth month of the year, in the fall. Every part was complete, just as it had been planned. It had taken Solomon seven years to build it.

decisions.choice: the month of Bul: the eighth month, October-November
decisions.reason: Bul is an old Canaanite month name, perhaps linked with rain or with the harvest of produce. The writer explains it as the eighth month, about October-November, later called Marcheshvan. The temple was dedicated at the feast in the seventh month (8:2), presumably of a later year.

decisions.choice: seven years: counted from the second month of the fourth year to the eighth month of the eleventh
decisions.reason: From Ziv of the fourth year to Bul of the eleventh is seven and a half years; the writer gives the round number.

decisions.choice: all its parts and all its plans: complete in every detail
decisions.reason: The first word means "matters" or "parts"; the second means its proper plan or specification. Together they say that nothing was left undone.

decisions.choice: that Solomon ruled; in the fall
decisions.reason: Readable says whose year it was and gives the season, as in verse 1.
